messages:
alex_infra: FYI - we started seeing containers lose GPU visibility after the nvidia-container-toolkit update in the new base image (us-west-2 AMI). Rolling canary finished ~09:12 and some pods show 0 GPUs available. @oncall?

lina_sre: I see this too. kube reports node allocatable for nvidia.com/gpu dropping from 8 -> 0 on a subset of g4dn hosts. Node-level `nvidia-smi` still works on the host, but inside container it's failing.

deploy-bot: canary-roll: toolkit-1.15 -> applied to 20 hosts in us-west-2 (09:05) :information_source:

raj_ml: sample error from a failing container run: 
```
2026-03-18T09:18:02Z stderr: could not open libnvidia-ml.so.1: No such file or directory
2026-03-18T09:18:02Z ERROR: GPU probe failed, treating as missing device
```

maria_platform: quick diff between 1.14 and 1.15 on the AMI: toolkit now installs a wrapper that prepends /opt/nvidia/lib to LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside the container rootfs at runtime. That path contains an older symlink layout which shadows the host /usr/lib/nvidia libs. Host modules and libs match driver 535 but the wrapped path points to 470-era names.

ryan_sre: can you paste the output of `ldd /usr/bin/nvidia-smi` from inside a failing container and `ls -l /opt/nvidia/lib` on the host? Also `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` on the host.

alex_infra: here's outputs from one of the affected nodes (redacted host id):
```
# host: ls -l /opt/nvidia/lib
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 18 Mar 18 08:50 libnvidia-ml.so.1 -> libnvidia-ml.so.470.199
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 16 Mar 18 08:50 libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.470.199
# container: ldd /usr/bin/nvidia-smi
	libnvidia-ml.so.1 => not found
	libcuda.so => not found
# host: cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 535.86.01 Wed Mar 16 2026
```

lina_sre: so wrapper is exposing older compat libs into the container rootfs before the host-provided bind mounts are applied. That would cause the in-container linker to pick the wrong ABI. Not all images mount `/usr/local/nvidia` the same way (some of our runtime images do late bind mounts).

maria_platform: Exactly. The new toolkit changed mount propagation defaults to RPRIVATE in some init scripts and copies a small libset into /opt/nvidia which then ends up earlier in the loader path. This is a subtle ordering race: if the host bind of /usr/lib/nvidia happens after the wrapper sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH, the container will load the stale libs.

ryan_sre: Impact: autoscaler reacted to unschedulable pods and spun up 5 extra nodes (09:27) in us-west-2 which briefly increased spend. I've cordoned and drained the affected nodes to stop noisy churn.

sre-bot: Automated action: cordon node ip-10-0-8-123 (09:31) ; drain initiated.

alex_infra: Mitigation plan: 1) Hotfix AMI: pin toolkit to 1.14 and rebuild image for us-west-2, 2) In parallel, add an init container that ensures host bind mounts happen before the toolkit wrapper runs (workaround script), 3) Open ticket with NVIDIA. Rolling rollback to previous AMI for 40 hosts now.

raj_ml: We validated rollback on one node: after switching AMI the container sees GPUs again and `nvidia-smi` inside container reports devices. Perf workloads resumed.

maria_platform: Also adding a short-term probe in our node-health check that runs `ldd /usr/bin/nvidia-smi` inside a debug container to detect library shadowing early. Will push the probe as a daemonset patch.

ryan_sre: Filing a support case with NVIDIA + attaching: kernel version, rpm/dpkg list, mount propagation change logs, and the `strace` of loader from a failing container. Please add any reproducer steps. I'll open the ticket and share the case id.

alex_infra: Notes for postmortem: root cause seems to be toolkit installer changing runtime wrapper behavior (LD_LIBRARY_PATH + pre-populated /opt/nvidia libs) combined with different bind-mount ordering on some of our container images. Secondary impact: cluster autoscaler overreacted -> cost spike (~$1.1k projected for the hour) and several customer workloads experienced transient OOMs while pods were rescheduled.

lina_sre: Follow-ups: - rollback complete for canary group, expanding to remaining hosts this afternoon - add test to AMI pipeline that brings up a sample container and verifies GPU visibility before promoting, - coordinate with infra release window to avoid autopromote during high-traffic hours.

maria_platform: Patch in progress: change toolkit init to use RSHARED mount propagation and defer wrapper LD changes until host binds are mounted. PR created: https://git.internal/repo/infra/patches/1234 (will request review).

deploy-bot: rollback-complete: toolkit pinned to 1.14 on 42 hosts (10:05) :white_check_mark:

ryan_sre: NVIDIA case opened #INC-2026-0427, vendor investigating. Keep this thread updated with reproducer and kernel logs.

alex_infra: Thanks all — keeping this open until vendor confirms fix and our AMI tests cover it. If you see anything else, drop it here. :thumbsup:
